Class Power Tuner

World of ClaudeCraft: operator reference and complete tunable surface.
Generated 2026-08-09 from the live content tables.

9classes, 27 specializations
308abilities
139weapon swing profiles
1545individual sliders

What this is

The Class Power Tuner is an operator-facing balance lever in the admin dashboard. It exposes every aspect of every ability of every class as a multiplier slider, plus the white-swing damage and swing timer of every weapon. Saved changes are stored per realm and applied to the world at the next server restart.

It exists because two of the nine classes have been reworked and now outperform the other seven. Closing that gap previously meant editing content source and shipping a build; with the tuner it is a slider and a restart.

Who can use it

Access is a dedicated staff role, tuner, carrying exactly two permissions: tuning.read (see the sliders and the change history) and tuning.write (save a document). The role carries nothing else: an account holding only tuner cannot see player accounts, act on players, or read the anti-bot internals, and every other admin endpoint answers it with 403. The permission is deliberately kept out of the read-only viewer bundle, so the balance surface reaches named people rather than every read-only seat.

Granting it:

node scripts/grant_admin.mjs <username> --roles tuner

How a change reaches the world

  1. A tuner moves sliders in the dashboard and saves, with a note explaining why.
  2. The document is validated, stored as one row per realm, and appended to an audit trail recording the before and after documents, the operator and the note. An unchanged save records nothing.
  3. The page reports the change as pending a restart. The running world is untouched.
  4. At the next server boot the document is installed onto the ability and item tables once, before the world is constructed. The realm then reports the saved and running documents as in sync.

Tuning is boot-scoped on purpose. Swapping ability values under a running world would change numbers underneath in-flight casts and cooldowns, and would leave the server and every connected client disagreeing for as long as the change took to propagate. The realm hands its installed document to each client in the connection handshake, so client tooltips, cooldown pips and cost predictions describe the numbers the server actually resolves.

How a slider works

Every slider is a multiplier from 0.10x to 3.00x in 0.01 steps, with 1.00x meaning "exactly as authored". The shipped values are always shown, and once a slider moves, the resulting values are shown beside them.

The multiplier is applied according to what the underlying number means, which is why the tool can be trusted with fields that are not plain magnitudes:

  • Magnitudes (damage, healing, seconds, yards, costs) scale directly. A whole number stays whole.
  • Multipliers whose neutral point is 1 (a snare's 0.5 speed multiplier, a 2x threat multiplier, a 1.4 haste aura) move by their distance from 1. Buffing a 50% snare by 20% makes it slow harder, not turn into a speed boost.
  • Normalized shares (a resurrect health fraction, a proc chance) scale and then clamp to at most the whole.
  • Marker auras (stance flags, one-shot empower tokens, form toggles) are never offered a slider: scaling a marker cannot help and can only break a predicate that reads it.

A slider that provably cannot change anything (a zero magnitude, a multiplier already at its neutral 1) is not rendered, so every control on the page does something.

Why the coverage stays complete

The tuner does not carry a hand-written list of knobs. One traversal of an ability definition both lists the sliders and applies them, so the controls offered and the numbers changed cannot drift apart, and the catalog the dashboard renders is derived from the live content tables. A reworked or brand-new class therefore appears with the right sliders the moment its content lands, with no dashboard work.

What keeps that honest is a guard test that walks every shipped ability and fails when it finds a numeric field the classification table does not account for, plus a second guard requiring every weapon the simulation reads to be present. A class rework that adds a new kind of number cannot quietly ship an untunable one: the build goes red until the field is classified.

The channel vocabulary

A channel is one aspect of an ability. The set is closed: every tunable number in the game is classified into exactly one of these, and a guard test fails the build if a class rework adds a number that fits none of them.

ChannelWhat it moves
Direct damage
damage_direct
Instant and cast damage: direct rolls, weapon-strike bonuses, weapon multipliers, imbue and judgement damage.
Damage over time
damage_dot
The total of a damage-over-time effect, and channelled drain ticks.
Area damage
damage_aoe
Area, chain, ground-zone, cone and orb damage.
Finisher damage
damage_finisher
Combo-point finisher damage: the base, the per-point scaling and its variance.
Reflect damage per hit
damage_reflect
Damage a thorns-style aura deals back per melee hit taken.
Direct healing
heal_direct
Direct, area and chain healing, plus percentage-of-health heals, leech shares and resurrect health fractions.
Healing over time
heal_hot
The total of a healing-over-time effect.
Absorb shielding
absorb
Shield amounts, including per-resource absorb rates.
Threat
threat
Flat bonus threat and the threat multiplier on an ability, per rank.
Spell power scaling
spell_power
A multiplier on the ability spell power / attack power coefficient. Offered only where something on the ability actually scales with power.
Resource cost
resource_cost
Rage, mana or energy cost per rank, spend caps, and self-damage costs.
Resource generated
resource_gain
Resource an ability grants: rage on interrupt or on area hits, mana from life tap, combo points awarded.
Cooldown
cooldown
The ability cooldown, and the internal cooldown of a charge-limited aura.
Cast time
cast_time
Cast time per rank and the total duration of a channel.
Aura and modifier strength
effect_magnitude
Aura, buff and debuff strength: attack power drains, damage-done percentages, haste and speed multipliers, snare strength, proc chances.
Effect duration
duration_effect
How long a beneficial or damage-over-time effect lasts: buffs, shields, zones, DoTs and HoTs.
Control duration
duration_control
How long an impairment lasts: stun, root, silence, fear, polymorph, incapacitate, snare, interrupt lockout.
Radius
radius
Area of effect radius, and cone angle.
Range
range
Cast range, including the minimum range of a ranged shot.
Distance
distance
Travel and displacement distances: blink, knockback, dash, and the boarball kicks.
Targets and charges
targets
Target counts and stack limits: chain jumps, maximum targets, dispel counts, sunder stacks, ability charges.
White swing damage
swing_damage
The minimum and maximum of a weapon auto-attack ("white") damage roll.
Swing timer
swing_speed
Seconds between auto-attack swings. Above 1 is slower, which lowers damage per second.
